description: Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware across the solar system–on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space. From rovers and instruments that completed their science missions to probes still traveling away from Earth this hardware varies widely in both its purpose and current level of functionality. Your challenge is to tell the story of some or all of this equipment that introduces school-age space enthusiasts to the hardware and the science it made possible.
summary:
The Forgotten Space Museum is an interactive digital museum. It explores the stories of spacecraft, rovers and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions ended. The website transforms these forgotten pieces of space exploration history into a virtual exhibition, allowing visitors to discover their purposes, mission ,scientific contributions, challenges and lasting legacies.

Through dedicated exhibition halls, visitors can explore missions of such spacecrafts , learn about the technology used in space exploration, discover where these artifacts are located  now and understand the discoveries they helped make. The website also incorporates interactive elements, educational content and quizzes to make learning engaging and accessible.

Its main purpose is to preserve the history of space exploration and remind visitors that even when a mission ends, its scientific contributions continue to matter.
details:
The Forgotten Space Museum is a virtual museum designed to make the history of space exploration more interactive and accessible. It focuses on the scientific equipment and spacecraft that remain on the surfaces of the Moon and Mars after their missions have ended.

The website is organised into themed exhibition halls, including the Red Planet, the Moon, Inside the Machines and the Legacy Gallery. Visitors can explore individual artifacts such as the Opportunity and Spirit rovers, the Phoenix lander, Sojourner and Surveyor 3. Each exhibit presents information about the machine's original purpose, mission history, scientific discoveries, engineering and final status.

The project aims to turn historical and scientific information into an engaging learning experience. Its interactive museum format encourages visitors to explore at their own pace rather than simply reading a collection of facts. It also highlights the lasting importance of missions that helped scientists understand other worlds and develop future exploration technologies.

The project was developed using Base44 for website creation and AI-assisted development, with AI tools used to organise the museum structure and develop written content. Canva was used for designing.

During development, I considered ease of navigation, visual design and the needs of visitors who may have little prior knowledge of space exploration. The futuristic museum concept was chosen to make the subject feel immersive while keeping the information understandable and educational.
